relations: Bare tile-chain legs hanging downward gain spheres at outer tips when a hand touches the bottom edge.
Inner legs tilt inward so their new spheres meet at center, forming a V before returning vertical.
Horizontal tile chains connect the lower spheres, converting the legs into vertical sides of three adjacent squares.
A hand adjusting the leftmost horizontal connection buckles the left square outward into a small triangular protrusion.
caption: The video showcases an overhead white surface holding a polished silver magnetic-tile lattice with a fixed upper truss panel and four lower legs being reshaped. Bare tile-chain legs hang downward until spheres appear at the outer tips, then at the inner tips, as a hand intermittently touches the bottom edge. The inner legs tilt inward so their new spheres meet at the center, forming a V before the legs appear vertical again. Horizontal tile chains connect the lower spheres, turning the legs into vertical sides of three adjacent squares. A hand adjusts the leftmost horizontal connection, and the left square later buckles outward into a small triangular protrusion. The upper X-braced panel remains in place while the lower framework continues shifting.
